threshold_notes: EPA 2012 RWQC (36/1000 illness rate): E. coli GM 126 / STV 410; enterococci GM 35 / STV 130 (32/1000 rate: GM 30/100, STV 110/320). Beach Action Value: E. coli 235 / enterococci 70 (precautionary notification). Fecal coliform: EPA 1976 Red Book recreational log-mean 200 (the national screen still used by EPA ECHO's Water Quality Indicators program); criterion-anchored to the E. coli GM (200 -> 126-equiv, factor 0.63). Enterococci convert to E.coli-equivalent at GM ratio 126/35 = 3.6x. MPN/CCE per 100 mL treated as CFU/100 mL for display (EPA WQI does the same). Total coliform deliberately excluded: drinking-water-oriented group with environmental species and no EPA recreational criterion. Values 700/1000/2000/5000 are documented order-of-magnitude extensions, not EPA criteria. Official advisories/closures take display priority over raw values where both exist.

indicators.role: EPA 1976 Red Book recreational indicator (ECHO/WQI screen)
indicators.conversion: x0.63 (criterion-anchored: Red Book 200 -> E. coli GM 126)

method_priority: official advisory/closure > STV exceedance > BAV exceedance > GM context > latest valid observation; overlaps resolve to highest concern; jurisdictional standards reconciled by mapping each to E.coli-equivalent and flagging the originating indicator in metadata samples.
unit_conversions: CFU/100 mL direct; MPN/100 mL ~= CFU/100 mL (display); enterococci x3.6 -> E.coli-equiv.
coverage: 100% of the five Great Lakes water surfaces (Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario; US + Canadian waters) via the shared NOAA shoreline mask; unrelated inland lakes excluded; land transparent.
canada_note: WQP covers US stations; Canadian/Ontario anchor beaches are listed and paint NO DATA until an ECCC/Ontario live feed is integrated (documented gap, upgrade path).
folder_html:
What This Shows

Available authoritative evidence of human-health-relevant bacterial/fecal contamination in Great Lakes recreational waters, as one unified concern spectrum (DARK BLUE, BLUE, CYAN, LIGHT GREEN, DARK GREEN, YELLOWISH GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, RED, NEON RED, MAGENTA, PURPLE, DARK PURPLE). Dark blue = no detected contamination / lowest measured condition; dark purple = extremely high contamination / extremely poor human-health water condition. Water without a live observation stays transparent (NO DATA — see the slate swatch in the key).

Source / Study

Measures: swim-water bacteria — E. coli, enterococci, and fecal coliform (CFU/100 mL) — from the USGS Water Quality Portal (WQX discrete samples, incl. state beach-program submissions) within EPA's BEACH/BEACON recreational-water framework.
Endpoints: https://www.waterqualitydata.us/ · EPA BEACON · EPA 2012 RWQC
Retrieval: WQP live query OK (1 usable samples); window 7 days ending 2026-10-07; 1 station halos from 27 anchor beaches.
Generation: build_bacteria.py; source version wqp-2026-10-07-n1-0350439.

How to Read the Gradient

Human-health concern from fecal-indicator evidence, FIXED log scale (E.coli-equiv CFU/100 mL): DARK BLUE 10 (no detected/lowest) → BLUE 30 (very low) → CYAN 60 (low) → LIGHT GREEN 100 (low-to-moderate) → DARK GREEN 126 (moderate, EPA GM) → YELLOWISH GREEN 190 (elevated) → YELLOW 235 (concerning, EPA Beach Action Value) → ORANGE 320 (high) → RED 410 (very high, EPA STV) → NEON RED 700 (extremely high) → MAGENTA 1000 (severe) → PURPLE 2000 (extremely severe) → DARK PURPLE HIGHEST+ 5000+ (extreme). LOWEST 10. Water without observations stays transparent (NO DATA, slate swatch in key) — never zero bacteria.

Why one spectrum: E. coli, enterococci, and fecal coliform are ALL routine swim-water bacterial tests for the same human-health question (is fecal contamination at levels of health concern?), so they are consolidated into one concern scale (enterococci ×3.6 = E.coli-equivalent via the EPA GM ratio; fecal coliform ×0.63 via criterion-anchoring to the Red Book 200 / E. coli GM 126) rather than mapped separately. No indicator is itself claimed to be a disease-causing pathogen in any sample, and the layer does not detect every pathogen.

Standards behind the colors: EPA 2012 RWQC — E. coli GM 126 / STV 410, enterococci GM 35 / STV 130, Beach Action Value E. coli 235 (notification level). Full per-color value/unit/threshold/source/rationale table is in metadata.json `thresholds`.

NO DATA ≠ zero: transparent water means no defensible observation exists there — it must never be read as clean water. A missing observation never becomes zero bacteria.

Coverage: the visual layer spans 100% of the five Great Lakes water surfaces (US + Canadian waters; unrelated inland lakes excluded; land transparent), while measured-data availability varies — most open water is honestly NO DATA because monitoring is beach- and station-based.

Data / Scientific Limitations

Water-quality indicator visualization, not a laboratory test of every part of the lake. Station-based samples; halos (radius 14px) show conditions NEAR a sampled station only — no interpolation between stations, no modeled fill. Samples older than 7 days are stale (NO DATA). Canadian waters list anchor beaches but currently paint NO DATA pending an ECCC/Ontario live feed. Advisories/closures take display priority where both exist.

Update Frequency

SOURCE CHECKED HOURLY (refreshInterval 3600 s on entry NetworkLink and overlay Icon), which is distinct from source publication frequency: agencies publish only when sampling occurs (often weekly in swim season). New samples are used when they appear; otherwise the latest valid observation is retained up to 7 days, then treated as stale.
